**ADI, 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-24: the quarter beat, and the stock is selling off on the fiscal 2027 setup.**

I ran 9 searches and opened 5 pages: the SEC 8-K press release, a StockTitan copy of it, an Investing.com call summary, a Substack analysis, and a Yahoo/JPMorgan conference piece. Two call-transcript pages (Benzinga, GuruFocus) returned 403 errors. I found no sell-side rating or price-target changes dated today.

**What happened (8-K, fiscal Q4 ended Oct 31)**
- Revenue was $4.37B, up 42% year over year, against a $4.3B guide and about $4.32B expected.
- Adjusted EPS was $4.06 against about $3.89 expected and a $3.86 guide. Adjusted operating margin was 52.3%.
- End markets, year over year:
  - Industrial: $2.19B, up 55%.
  - Communications: $707M, up 81%. Data center is about 83% of that segment and more than doubled for a second straight quarter.
  - Automotive: $1.04B, up 21%.
  - Consumer: $429M, up 7%.
- Fiscal 2026 revenue was $15.2B, up 38%, with $5.45B of free cash flow.
- ADI declared a $1.10 dividend with a record date of Dec 7 and payment on Dec 21.

**Why it is falling (the sources say this is inference, not company statements)**
- **Q1 guide:**
  - Revenue is $4.4B, plus or minus $150M, only about 1% above Q4.
  - Adjusted EPS is $3.82, below Q4's $4.06.
  - Adjusted operating margin is about 50.5%, down from 52.3%.
  - Gross margin is about 74%, down from 74.5%, because of holiday fab shutdowns.
  - Operating expenses are guided up by a mid-single-digit percentage, including a full quarter of Alif Semiconductor.
  - Nonoperating expense is about $90M against $37M in Q4.
  - Part of the EPS drop is therefore non-operating, not demand.
- **Capex:** Fiscal 2027 capex is $1.6B to $1.9B, against $733M in fiscal 2026. It goes to clean rooms in Europe and the US and to back-end test and assembly. New capacity arrives from about Q1 fiscal 2028. Management says capex falls back toward 4% to 6% of revenue in 2028. It expects free cash flow to rise, and it expects some CHIPS Act tax credits.
- **Near-term mix:**
  - Consumer is guided down 10% to 15% sequentially on memory-related headwinds and seasonality.
  - Automotive is guided down low single digits sequentially.
  - Communications decelerated sequentially, and management cited wireless softness.
- **Inventory:** Inventory is up 26% year over year to $2.08B, and days of inventory rose to 165. Management says this is a die bank for high-demand parts, and channel inventory is within its 6-to-7-week target.
- **Valuation and positioning:** The stock was up about 60% over twelve months. The 52-week high is $445.91 and the low is $229.29. A note from earlier this week listed semiconductors as the most crowded trade in a Bank of America fund manager survey, but I couldn't date it.

**Offsetting points from the call**
- Management says order books are strong and design wins are at a record.
- It says it is mid-cycle, with normal cancellation activity and no material customer restocking.
- Supply is tight, but packaging bottlenecks are improving monthly.
- Management described the Q1 guide as above seasonal. It declined to give full-year fiscal 2027 guidance.
- An earlier CFO comment pointed to double-digit growth into fiscal 2027. That article is from September, so it predates this report.
- Analysts asked whether the Q1 guide is conservative.

- It was down 17.75% premarket, at $311.51.
- Intraday range as of the StockTitan snapshot is $304.23 to $374.01. The Substack snapshot had it at $307.80, down 18.7%.
- At $316.68 it is down about 16.4%, so it has bounced a little off the low.
- StockTitan showed volume at about 4 times normal at its snapshot. Your screen projects 2.4 times for the full day.

**What could move it over the next 1 to 10 sessions**
- **Today's close:** A bounce off the $304 low into the close would show buyers stepping in. A close at the low would suggest continuation.
- **Analyst notes:** Price-target moves and any downgrades on the capex and margin story will come over the next 1 to 2 days. Notes defending the beat and calling the guide conservative could support a rebound.

**Read:** The business is strong, with a clean beat and record data-center growth. The sell-off reflects a flat Q1 guide, margin and EPS stepping down, and a capex jump, after a large run-up. **Dycom (DY), Tuesday 2026-11-24, about 12:10 PM CT. The stock is down about 16.5% to roughly 182 after a fiscal Q3 2027 beat and a soft Q4 guide.**

I ran 9 searches and opened 6 pages. The first was Dycom's own 8-K press release on SEC.gov. The other five were Investing.com, the Trefis piece, the Finviz/StockStory piece, the Benzinga article and the MarketScreener page. Benzinga and Chartmill returned 403, and MarketScreener returned no content.

I found no transcript of today's call, no analyst reactions today, and no Q4 consensus figures. Numbers from the Investing.com article are AI-assisted, so I checked them against the release where I could.

**What the press release says (from the 8-K)**
- **Revenue and EPS:** Revenue was $2.056B, up 41.6% but only 11.2% organically. Adjusted EPS was $5.23 against an estimate of about $4.59. GAAP EPS was $3.19, down 12.1%.
- **Backlog:** Record $12.91B, up 57%. The next-12-months portion was $6.7B, up from $5.0B.
- **Margin pressure in Communications:** Segment adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 12.8% from 15.1%. The company blamed scaling costs and higher fuel prices. Organic Communications growth was 11.2%. Building Systems, which came from the Power Solutions acquisition, earned a 23.8% margin.
- **Customer credit:** A rural customer filed Chapter 11 and another smaller customer is in financial difficulty. Dycom took a $22.7M reserve, or $0.57 per share after tax.
- **Guidance:** The full-year revenue range is $7.66B to $7.73B. Q4 guidance is revenue of $1.63B to $1.70B, adjusted EBITDA of $204M to $218M and adjusted EPS of $2.48 to $2.78. Q4 was reported as below the Street, but I couldn't confirm by how much.
- **Cash:** Cash fell to $203M from $709M at the start of the year. Debt is about $2.8B, so net debt is roughly $2.6B. Receivables rose to $2.53B from $1.70B.

**Why it is falling**
- **Q4 guide below consensus:** Benzinga's headline attributes the drop to guidance. The Q4 EBITDA guide of $204M to $218M is well below this quarter's $312M. Part of that is seasonal, but it needs checking against the Street's number.
- **FTTH outlook (reported, not confirmed):** Investing.com says management signaled fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) revenue may decline in fiscal 2028 from fiscal 2027, while staying above fiscal 2026. Its other fiscal 2028 points were mid-single-digit growth in Communications and high-teens or better growth in Building Systems. I didn't see this on a call transcript.
- **Cash flow:** Operating cash flow was $14M, against $220M a year ago. Free cash flow was about -$33M, and days sales outstanding rose to 112 from 105. Management reportedly expects "several hundred million dollars" of operating cash flow in Q4.
- **Buyback:** Dycom repurchased $100.5M of stock in the quarter. One source mentions a new $200M authorization, and I couldn't verify it.

**Backdrop**
- **Earlier declines:** The stock peaked near $566 in 2026 and was already down about 42% over three months by late August. The Q2 report on August 26 beat estimates but gave a soft Q3 revenue midpoint, attributed to capacity investment and wireless projects deferred into fiscal 2028. A Trefis piece described a nine-day losing streak of 32% around then.
- **Customer concentration:** AT&T and Verizon each exceeded 10% of revenue in Q2.
- **Acquisitions:** Power Solutions closed on December 23, 2025 for about $2.0B of total consideration. The National Technology Integrators acquisition (about $275M, also in Building Systems) closed in fiscal Q2 2027.
- **Analysts:** Ratings were still mostly Buy as of July. Some analysts cut price targets after Q2. I found no post-earnings target changes yet.

**What could move it over the next 1 to 10 sessions**
- **Downside:**
  - Analyst target cuts and downgrades over the next day or two.
  - Continued forced selling from momentum and growth holders.
  - More credit problems, given receivables up 49% and negative free cash flow.
  - Any confirmation that FTTH is shrinking in fiscal 2028.
- **Upside:**
  - A quick rebound from an oversold level: 5.1 times normal volume, a break below the 52-week low, and about 17% of the decline coming in one day.
  - Buyback support.
  - Backlog growth of 57% and a book-to-bill of 1.3, which don't fit a thesis of collapsing demand.
  - Data-center demand: long-haul and data center interconnect backlog reportedly doubled to over $2B.
  - Management's promise of a Q4 cash inflow, with the next test being the fiscal Q4 report in early March.
- **Key uncertainty:** The story turns on whether the selling is about FTTH peaking and margin compression, which would be a lasting reset, or about guidance conservatism, which would be a reaction that fades. I couldn't settle that without the call transcript or the Street's Q4 numbers.

**Summary:** DOW is a leveraged bet on US polyethylene (PE) prices. Dow nominated large November PE price increases, and the market doubts they will stick. That doubt, plus a likely oil-and-ethane unwind, is probably why the stock is down 14% in 20 days. The bounce today has no news behind it that I could find. I found nothing from after about Nov 16, so the drop's exact trigger is unconfirmed.

**The story**
- **Q3 (Oct 22):** Sales were $11.3B, up 13%. Operating EPS was $0.71 against a loss of $0.19 a year ago. Operating EBIT was $887M. Free cash flow was $1.1B. Volume fell 1%, mostly because Middle East supply was constrained. Dow also trimmed its 2026 self-help EBITDA uplift target to "more than $1B", down from more than $1.3B last quarter.
- **Beat or miss:** Sources disagree. Earnings Whispers calls it a miss against a $0.64 consensus, while Zacks and others frame it as a beat. I couldn't settle this.
- **Q4 guide:** EBITDA of about $1.5B, roughly flat on Q3.
  - If the October (7 cents/lb) and November (5 cents/lb) PE increases fully stick, Dow sees about $200M of upside. Each 1 cent/lb is worth about $50M per quarter.
  - The guide assumes ethane in the mid-to-high 20s cents/gal.
- **Cash and balance sheet:** About $14B of liquidity and no substantive maturities until 2029. Dow is buying back debt ($300M in Q3, about $200M planned for Q4). The quarterly dividend is $0.35. It was halved in July 2025, and the ex-dividend date is Nov 30, so a small mechanical drop (about 1.2%) is coming.
- **Why the stock ran up earlier:** The Iran war began in late February and constrained Middle East petrochemical capacity. PE rose about 24% in the war's first weeks. Dow and LyondellBasell benefit because they run on cheap North American ethane.
- **Why it can drop hard:** On Apr 17, DOW fell about 10% in a day on news that Iran said the Strait of Hormuz was open. The stock trades as a war and supply-shock proxy.
- **Longer-term overhang:**
  - Global operating rates are in the low 80s percent, and Dow says about 10% of capacity must close to reach mid-cycle levels. About half of that is announced.
  - New Chinese capacity is growing.
  - MDI (a polyurethane chemical) is weak because building and construction demand is weak.
  - The Sadara JV (Saudi Arabia) is still partly down. Dow has capped its funding at about $1.3B.
  - Analysts on the call asked whether PE prices hold in 2027 if the Middle East normalizes.
  - Dow gave no 2027 EBITDA number.
- **Analysts:** Consensus is Hold or Neutral, with targets mostly $30 to $40. Recent actions I found are UBS Hold with a $30 target (Sep 25) and Deutsche Bank Hold with a $32 target (Sep 17). BofA moved to Underperform in April. I found no November rating changes.

**What could move it over the next 1 to 10 sessions**
- **November PE contract settlement (the main swing factor):** S&P Global reported on Oct 30 that producers were split on whether the 5 to 7 cent November increases would hold, given the typical Q4 inventory sell-off. A PlasticsToday piece dated Nov 16 had producers still pushing 5 cents. I found no settlement report. The 14% slide suggests the market expects a partial or failed increase. A report of a flat or partial settlement is a downside risk. A report that most of it stuck is the upside catalyst.
- **December nominations:** These would come around month-end.
- **Oil, ethane and Iran/Hormuz headlines:** Falling oil or a firm US-Iran deal hits DOW. A breakdown in talks helps it.
- **Nov 30 ex-dividend date.**

**The story.** HALO is a royalty company with strong fundamentals. Its drop is a patent-and-expectations selloff, not a business problem.

- **Business.** Halozyme licenses ENHANZE, an enzyme that lets partners turn IV drugs into under-the-skin injections. Q3 2026, reported Nov 5:
  - Revenue was $493M, up 39%.
  - Royalties were a record $341M, up 44%.
  - Non-GAAP EPS was $2.39, against a $2.28 consensus.
  - 2026 guidance was raised, with royalties now $1.235–1.255B and non-GAAP EPS $8.75–9.05.
  - The balance sheet is heavier: about $3.25B of debt after a $1.5B convertible issue, against $1.08B of cash.
  - Buybacks total $400M for 2026. Q3 buybacks averaged $79.47 a share.
- **Why the stock fell.** HALO ran about 45% after the August report and hit a 52-week high of $134 on Oct 30. The Q3 beat and raise were small. On Nov 6 it fell about 15% (from $122.96 to about $104.75). Leerink cut it to Market Perform that day but raised its target to $117, citing the run-up, limited outlook improvement and uncertainty over Keytruda royalties.
- **The Merck fight.** Merck's subcutaneous Keytruda (Keytruda Qlex) uses Alteogen's enzyme, not ENHANZE. Halozyme says that enzyme infringes its separate MDASE patents. MDASE earns no royalties today, and Halozyme says the case doesn't touch ENHANZE. The market is pricing the lost chance of future royalties. Keytruda Qlex had $830M of Q3 sales, and Merck targets 30–40% of US Keytruda patients on it by end-2027.
  - **US.** This front is bad for Halozyme. The patent appeals board (PTAB) has issued 11 final decisions finding every challenged claim unpatentable, and reviews of the last three patents were accepted in September. Halozyme has filed four appeals and management expects them to run to about 2028. The New Jersey infringement case is waiting on that process.
  - **Europe.** A Hague court ruled for Halozyme on Oct 7 and enjoined Keytruda SC in eight countries. On Nov 19, a German higher court overturned the Munich preliminary injunction, and HALO fell about 4.5% to about $92 (the seventh straight down day). Halozyme says it will file a new German suit for permanent relief. The Dutch ruling is unaffected.
  - **UK.** Halozyme accepted revocation of the main patent (EP622) there in May 2026. A trial on a second patent starts Nov 30.
- **Other risks.**
  - Three products (Darzalex, Vyvgart Hytrulo, Phesgo) make up 81% of royalties, and Darzalex alone is 45%.
  - The US Darzalex royalty steps down from September 2027, possibly delayed to March 2029 if a reissue patent is granted.
  - Alteogen's partners are growing competition.
- **Valuation.** One Substack author puts the stock at about 10x 2026 profit. Their bear case implies about $93, close to today's price. That is one author's view, not a consensus.

**Dycom (DY): research as of 12:10 PM CT, Tuesday 11/24/2026**

**Bottom line:** The quarter beat and backlog hit a record. The stock is down about 16% because management told the Street that fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) work will shrink in fiscal 2028 (the year starting Feb 2027). The sell-off is a reset of the long-term story, not a one-quarter miss.

**What happened**
- **Q3 beat (quarter ended 10/31):** Revenue was $2.056B, up 41.6% (11.2% organic), above the $1.90–1.98B guide. Adjusted EPS was $5.23 against about $4.56 expected. Adjusted EBITDA was $311.7M (15.2% margin). [SEC release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000067215/000006721526000048/dyfy2027q3earningsreleasee.htm)
- **Record backlog:** Total backlog is $12.9B, up 57%, with $6.7B expected in the next 12 months.
- **Full-year raise:** Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance is now $7.66–7.73B, up roughly $125M at the midpoint.
- **Weak Q4 guide (quarter ending Jan 2027):** Revenue is $1.63–1.70B, adjusted EBITDA $204–218M and adjusted EPS $2.48–2.78. That is a bit under the roughly $2.71–2.76 consensus. Management blamed holidays, short days and winter weather. Q4 also has 13 weeks against 14 last year. [Stockanalysis transcript](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/dy/transcripts/739233-q3-2027/)
- **The main cause, FTTH slowing in fiscal 2028:**
  - Several large, unnamed customers "in recent weeks" decided to moderate their build pace.
  - FTTH revenue is expected to fall in fiscal 2028 from fiscal 2027, though it stays above fiscal 2026.
  - Management said regional overbuilders have stopped building, partly because of higher cost of capital.
  - Management said consumers are not switching from fiber to satellite.
- **Fiscal 2028 outlook:** Communications revenue is guided to grow only mid-single digits. Long-haul and data-center interconnect should lead growth, and Building Systems should grow in the high teens or better. The mid-single-digit figure was questioned on the call. Management said it has some upside built in and that BEAD (the federal rural broadband funding program) is still uncertain. Formal fiscal 2028 guidance comes with Q4 results, probably in March.

**Other negatives**
- **Margins:** Communications margin fell to 12.8% from 15.1% a year ago, on scaling costs and fuel (about 50 bps from fuel). The prior quarter was 13.6%.
- **Receivables charge:** A $22.7M reserve ($0.57 per share, excluded from adjusted EPS) covers a rural customer in Chapter 11 and another troubled smaller customer. Neither had Q3 revenue or has backlog.
- **Cash and debt:** Days sales outstanding were 112. Cash fell to $203M from $709M in January. Total debt is about $2.8B, and quarterly interest expense is $39M, up from $14M. Management said pro forma net leverage is about 2.3x and expects "several hundred million" of operating cash flow in Q4 as receivables normalize. Customer mergers were slowing collections. That is a claim to check against Q4 results.

**Supports for the stock**
- **Buyback:** It bought $100.5M of stock in Q3 (345,000 shares). A new $200M authorization runs through May 2028.
- **Analysts and insiders:** Most analysts are still Buy-rated (9 Buy, 3 Hold) with stale high targets. Wells Fargo cut its target from $550 to $300 and kept Overweight. Directors bought about $300K of stock in September at $281–287, which is far above today's price. [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-dycom-industries-nyse-dy-reaches-new-1-year-low-whats-next-2026-11-24/)
- **Valuation:** The market cap is about $5.6B at around 16x trailing earnings.

**Context**
- This is the second guidance-driven drop in three months. On 8/26 the stock fell about 13% on a soft Q3 guide, partly from about $150M of wireless revenue pushed into fiscal 2028. The company also announced a $150M buyback then. [FinancialContent/StockStory](https://www.financialcontent.com/article/stockstory-2026-8-26-why-dycom-dy-shares-are-sliding-today)
- The stock was about $282 on 10/7 and $207 on 11/6, and its high was $566. Part of the slide was a broader sell-off in AI and data-center infrastructure names. [Tickeron](https://tickeron.com/blogs/dycom-industries-dy-shares-fall-26-5-in-30-days-as-guidance-weighs-on-sentiment-31299/)
- Dycom is about 98% institutionally owned and has a beta of about 1.5.

**What could move it over the next 1–10 sessions**
- **Downside:**
  - Analyst target cuts and downgrades, which are likely over the next day or two.
  - Forced selling from momentum and growth funds.
  - Naming of the customers slowing builds (AT&T, Verizon and Lumen are the largest, but none was named). A named AT&T or Verizon cut would hit hard.
  - Further read-through from other fiber contractors and customers.
  - Year-end tax-loss selling.
- **Upside:**
  - A bounce from a deeply oversold, 52-week-low print on record backlog.
  - Buyback support.
  - Dip buying by analysts who stay Buy-rated.
  - Any customer commentary that the slowdown is a pause.
  - Insider buying after the report.
- **Not expected soon:** No scheduled company catalyst before Q4 results in early March.
